newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe's Mugabe opens world solar conference.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe's Mugabe opens world solar conference.

text.p: An international conference on solar and other renewable sources of energy opened in Harare on Monday, with host Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe appealing for solid political and financial support for its development.

The two-day World Solar Summit is being attended by 10 heads of state and governments and delegates from more than 100 countries and was called to drum up support for a programme aimed at providing secure energy to 2.4 billion people living without electricity worldwide.

In his opening address, Mugabe appealed to the international community to offer all-round political and financial backing to a World Solar Programme prepared by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO) to boost the use of solar, wind, geothermal and other renewable sources of energy.
"There is need for governments and the private sector to support this programme fully," he said, emphasising the targeted sources were cheaper than most sources of energy currently in use.
About 300 projects falling under UNESCO's 1996-2005 World Solar Programme are due to be presented to the summit, jointly organised by UNESCO and Zimbabwe.
